land.text: Tripoli, the Hafsid city taken by Pedro Navarro in 1510

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Hafsid dynasty as the preceding authority. The Hafsid dossier records the loss to crown-of-castile.

land.text: Tripoli, accepted as a fief by the Knights Hospitaller on 23 March 1530 and taken over on 25 July

successors.note: Charles V had offered Tripoli, Malta and Gozo to the Order after its expulsion from Rhodes in 1522.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: A presidio under the Spanish Viceroy of Sicily; Pedro Navarro was first ruler (1510) and François Velasquès last (1520-1530) on the infobox. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the walled city of Tripoli, with a hinterland 'only intermittently present' within about 16 km

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Spanish control remained tenuous and it was never fully secured'; the Spanish authority was 'only intermittently present' within 10 miles (16 km) of the city. The 25 km circle is the grid's minimum.

ledger.note: 25 July 1510: Pedro Navarro captures Tripoli. The infobox lists 'Spanish conquest: 25 July 1510'; the text: the city 'was captured by Spanish forces in July 1510', led by Count Pedro Navarro. It became a presidio under the Spanish Viceroy of Sicily.

25 July 1530: the Hospitallers take control. They 'accepted the city as a fief on 23 March 1530' and 'took control of the city on 25 July' (infobox: Hospitaller fief 23 March 1530; Disestablished 25 July 1530).
1530: Spanish rule ends. The Hospitaller Tripoli page: 'Tripoli had been under Spanish rule since its capture in 1510'; the Order accepted Tripoli, Malta and Gozo as a fief on 23 March 1530.

wars.name: Tajura resistance to Spanish rule
wars.outcome: 'The sheikh escaped to Tajura in 1526, which subsequent became a base for Muslim resistance against Spanish rule.'
wars.note: Only 1526 is dated; the end year is the state's end. The page also has Barbary pirates plan an attack in 1512 and threats rising after Oruc Reis and Hayreddin took Algiers from Spain in 1515.

certainty.note: One walled city; the page gives no extent and the 25 km circle is the grid's minimum.

notes: Cliopatria has no Tripoli row for 1510-1551: the Hafsid Dynasty row carries Tripolitania to 1551 (Hafsid dossier, note 2), which is the overlap to correct. The Hafsid dossier writes the 1510 loss with the counterpart crown-of-castile; this dossier is the state the Spanish held it through. The Hafsid dossier cites the Siege of Tripoli page for 'under Spanish rule since its capture in 1510'; this one rests on the Spanish Tripoli and Hospitaller Tripoli pages.
